title: GTA 6 Doesn’t Compromise Scale For Detail, Rockstar Says
description: Rockstar's games are known for their impressive attention to detail, along with their massive scopes, and GTA 6 is seemingly going to up the ante in that regard. Rockstar boss Aaron Garbut said in an interview that a developer might compromise scale for detail or detail for interaction "but not with this project." "We went the other way," he told Game Informer. "Everything is dialed up--detail, scope, breadth, scale, interaction, and density." He went on to say Rockstar has never "created anything close to this before." "As the pressure for us on this project is huge, we dealt with that by doing our best to overdeliver," Garbut said. Lucia and Jason in GTA 6.No game can have everything, though, and GTA 6 is no different. The game takes place in Florida stand-in Leonida but doesn't feature Walt Disney World, for example, but Rockstar says the game will deliver the "full Florida experience." GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. The game has reportedly already sold close to 6 million copies, generating more than $570 million in pre-sales. Also this week, Rockstar revealed that GTA 6 will have more than 170 animal species, including cane toads and monkeys. We also learned that GTA 6 has a new dynamic weather system.

title: Former Steelers Head Coach Reveals Minecraft City He’s Been Building For 12 Years
description: Mike Tomlin served as head coach of the Pittsburgh Steelers from 2007-2025, which is a remarkably long tenure in the NFL. During more than half of that time, Tomlin was secretly working on a massive Minecraft city, and he's now revealing it to the general public. In the first episode of his deep dive into the Minecraft city--and the first video on his YouTube channel--Tomlin shared how the city began, initially with his kids' participation, but as they grew older, it became more and more of a focus for him alone. Much like the Steelers' roster changed every season, Tomlin remained the constant. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_h_pQ1-5iQg As you can see in the video, Mike Tomlin put an enormous amount of effort and time into building this city, not only creating the skyscrapers and nearby neighborhoods, but also sports stadiums. He said in the first episode that he'd go into more detail on these stadiums later, but the city includes a baseball field and a soccer pitch, alongside the obvious football field. His son Mayce also shared that Tomlin would sometimes take his PlayStation, presumably due to a sudden creative spark. https://twitter.com/maycetomlin/status/2105457694148821231 Tomlin has a lot more time to focus on Minecraft since resigning as the Steelers' head coach following the 2025 season. During his tenure, the team famously never had a losing season, which might just change this year with a grandfather at quarterback and a defense that has major issues stopping the run. Pittsburgh native Mike McCarthy is the team's new head coach, and it's unclear if he plays Minecraft.

title: PUBG: Black Budget Canceled, Joining Live-Service Graveyard
description: PUBG publisher Krafton has pulled the plug on its extraction shooter spin-off PUBG: Black Budget. Announced less than a year ago and already through several closed alpha tests, the publisher's reasoning for the cancellation is simple: it believes Black Budget simply wasn't fun enough to keep potential players engaged. "After reviewing the project's development status and future direction, we concluded that its current direction would not allow us to deliver an experience players could enjoy over the long term," Krafton wrote in a Steam update. "We have therefore made the difficult decision to end development of PUBG: Black Budget. PUBG Studios will carry what we learned from development and testing into future projects, continuing to listen to players as we explore new gameplay experiences." Black Budget is the second PUBG spin-off to get the axe, following the demise of the tactical shooter PUBG: Blindspot in March. While the game launched in early access, Krafton closed it down after two months, saying it was "no longer able to sustainably provide the level of experience" it set out to deliver. PUBG: Black BudgetKrafton's reasons for cancelling Black Budget aren't without merit. If it had been fully released, Black Budget would likely have faced an uphill battle, as the extraction shooter genre is perceived as a niche market dominated by a handful of games, while the live-service video game graveyard is full of recent projects that failed to find an audience. Many games launch with strong momentum, but they struggle to retain those initial player numbers, and their audiences shrink quickly. Just look at Highguard, as the free-to-play shooter lasted just over a month before it shut down. PUBG franchise director Taeseok Jang recently reflected on the struggles of Highguard and other live-service games, commenting on how hard it is to succeed in that space. Krafton has another PUBG spin-off in the works, the grindhouse-themed multiplayer shooter Ded.Net. Announced back in August during Gamescom, it's currently being developed by Krafton's Wisconsin-based studio PUBG Madison.

title: Uncharted 5 Is Reportedly In Development And Will Feature Nathan Drake
description: Naughty Dog is focused on releasing its first new IP since 2013's The Last of Us in Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, but a new report suggests it is also busy with the revival of its biggest franchise. According to MP1st, and corroborated by VGC, Naughty Dog could be developing Uncharted 5, a sequel to a series that last saw an entry in 2017. The report claims that Uncharted: The Lost Legacy director Shaun Escayag is leading the project, after briefly leaving Naughty Dog to work on Crystal Dynamic's ill-fated Avengers. It's suggested that Uncharted 5 will be the studio's next release after Intergalactic, with The Last of Us 3 coming afterwards. That would align with Naughty Dog's recent announcement that it is working on multiple new Last of Us projects. The report doesn't have too many details on the game itself, outside of mentioning that the series' main protagonist, Nathan Drake, will be present in some capacity. That could leave the door open for Cassie Drake, Nathan's daughter who appears at the end of Uncharted: 4 A Thief's End, to potentially take over as the series' lead going forward. This latest entry is also apparently not a remake of any sort, with Naughty Dog reportedly shelving those plans a long time ago. Uncharted 4 was positioned as the definitive end for Nathan Drake's story when it released in 2016, but Naughty Dog has repeatedly suggested that it is not done with the franchise. Escayag himself stated in 2022 that it's a world the studio wants to see more of, saying “I think we can say for certain that we can never say never." In February of this year, he posted a vague Instagram photo of a cannon in a tropical environment that was captioned “research," suggesting that he might be working on something related to Uncharted. When Uncharted 5 might release is anyone's guess, but it's more likely that it'll arrive on the PlayStation 6 given that Sony is expected to release its next-generation console sometime in 2028. Intergalatic, the studio's most imminent project, will be revealed in full in 2027, with a release window still unknown.

title: Xbox Is Paying A Lot Less Than Normal For Kojima’s Physint, Possibly Under $200 Million – Report
description: New Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has made a lot of big moves since taking over for Phil Spencer in the role, one of which was signing Hideo Kojima's new spy-thriller game, Physint, after Sony walked away from it. According to The New York Times, Xbox's agreement with Kojima was "substantially below what Xbox would typically spend to develop a premium game." What exactly would be typical, however, is unknown, because game studios are incredibly secretive about budgets. The money figures for Physint have been a point of contention, with unconfirmed reports that Physint's budget at Sony was $400 million. This has never been confirmed, but it was also reported that one of the reasons Sony opted to drop Kojima and Physint was that the game was over budget and late. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NzzdyORdg80 Windows Central's Jez Corden said he was told by first-hand sources with "direct knowledge of the contracts" for Physint at Xbox that the real number is "far lower." He said the deal between Xbox and Kojima amounts to only a "fraction" of the reported figure. The Game Business reporter Chris Dring, who originated the $400 million rumor, said he was only speculating, and the internet did what the internet does. He subsequently stated that he understands that Xbox is paying "far, far less," and "possibly even below $200 million." Xbox's deal with Kojima for Physint also covers film and TV adaptations. Physint stars Bill Skarsgard as its lead, along with Charlee Fraser, Don Lee, and Minami Hamabe. The game doesn't have a release date or any footage as of yet. Kojima believes Physint could become his most commercial game yet. Kojima said he got the idea for Physint in part due to the overwhelming fan demand for another Metal Gear game. He no longer works at Konami and couldn’t make a new Metal Gear, but the interest from fans inspired him to make a “new action espionage game” that became Physint. Sony originally announced that it would publish Physint, but the company told Kojima over Zoom that it was terminating the deal. Kojima's previous game franchise with Sony, Death Stranding, reportedly barely broke even. Sharma also briefly discussed Xbox's relationship with PlayStation, saying the two companies currently work together and that will continue under her leadership. "Competition and collaboration can coexist," she said. Physint is not the only Kojima game that Xbox is publishing, as the company is also partnered with the studio for the horror game OD.

title: The Witcher 3 Remastered Is Already Being Patched For Being Too Bright
description: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered launched for free earlier this week, and has since been subject to debate over whether its visual changes have been for the better. One aspect that has routinely dominated the conversation is how overly bright the remaster makes the game look, and it's evident developer CD Projekt Red agrees that it went too far. A patch for Xbox Series X|S, PlayStation 5, and the Xbox Play Anywhere version of the game on PC has been released that makes "various lighting adjustments" across the game, among other things. CD Projekt Red detailed the patch on social media, stating that the team is working on another hotfix for PC that will address a save game issue that numerous players have reported. The brief patch notes can be found below. https://youtu.be/_oEdB5S2d3U?si=v_wBtlRpVoS4Waq- Fixed an issue where DLSS was unavailable in the Xbox Play Anywhere version of the game on PC Made various lighting adjustments, including fixing some interiors that appeared too dark Made various other adjustments to ensure parity with the PC version The patch isn't being released for other PC versions because it's likely that the fix centers around the game's bloom setting. It's one that PC players have suggested turning off to regain some contrast in the game's image, but one that wasn't available for players on consoles. A different hotfix released on October 1 has a slightly different list of notes: Fixed an issue where the game couldn't be saved or loaded if the path to the Documents folder contained special characters. Fixed an issue where voiceover audio could become significantly quieter than other in-game audio after navigating through the pause menu tabs. Made various visual adjustments in Velen, including tweaks to Bloom, vegetation lighting, saturation, and Path Tracing lighting. Reverted a change that caused significant performance and visual issues with HairWorks enabled for some users. Fixed an issue where marketing telemetry settings weren't saved properly. Fixed an issue where it wasn't possible to launch the Classic (1.32) version of the game. This patch doesn't introduce a toggle, but likely toggles it off for all console players. If you're playing on Nintendo Switch 2, however, you won't be able to benefit from the fix just yet. The bloom setting doesn't fix everything though. Players have still taken issue with the game's HDR implementation, path tracing visual presentation, and overall system performance on PC. CD Projekt Red hasn't yet commented on whether it is planning to make changes to those areas, but this patch does indicate that they are aware of the most glaring issues players are facing. The Witcher 3 Remastered released as a free update for all versions of the game, introducing enhanced character animations, world detail, improved combat and role-playing systems, and more. An expansion for the 11 year old game, Songs of the Past, is scheduled to release in 2027 and will tie into the events of the The Witcher 4, which is currently in development.

title: Resident Evil Director’s Next Movie Is Called The Flood But It’s Not About Halo, Adds Jennifer Lawrence
description: Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie is a critical and commercial hit, but the director is not jumping right into a sequel, and may never. Instead, his next project is called The Flood, and while The Flood are well-known to gamers in Halo's lore, Cregger's new movie has nothing to do with Halo--though it does involve aliens. Cregger is known for keeping secrets about his movies, and he’s not saying much about what to expect from The Flood beyond that it’s a sci-fi movie set in deep space. Dread Central reported that The Flood is "very Alien-esque," with the story focusing on a deep-space ship captain who, with her crew, investigates a strange signal "from a distant world." The signal leads the crew to an "alien artifact that warps time, reality, and their sanity, forcing them into a confrontation with an incomprehensible intelligence." Oscar-winning actor Jennifer Lawrence has signed on for The Flood, according to Variety. Though her exact role in the film remains unknown, she will likely play the lead, the ship captain. This is somewhat familiar ground for Lawrence, as she starred in 2016's sci-fi movie Passengers, in which she played a character aboard a spaceship opposite Chris Pratt. Cregger is re-teaming with Warner Bros./New Line for The Flood; he previously made the successful thriller Weapons at the studio. He said in a statement that Lawrence is a "one-of-a-kind" talent and that he's excited to work with her. In addition to Warner Bros./New Line, Cregger is working with Steven Spielberg's Amblin Entertainment and Roy Lee's Vertigo on The Flood. As for Lawrence, she earned her first Academy Award nomination for 2010's Winter's Bone. She won an Oscar for 2012's Silver Linings Playbook, and also picked up nominations for American Hustle and Joy. She is also known for playing Katniss in the Hunger Games movie series. As for a possible sequel to Resident Evil, given the movie has made so much money and strong reviews, many are expecting another entry. That may happen, but Cregger has said he is done with franchise movies, even though he does have ideas for a sequel. “I’m doing this [Resident Evil], and that’s it for me. I’m not going to go tackle any other franchises," he said.

title: 007 First Light’s Free Expansion Gives Bond A Driving License To Kill
description: 007 First Light developer IO Interactive has revealed a major new free update for the James Bond game, which is now available across PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X|S. Extended Operations adds new missions, the Valhalla Protocol, a photo mode, New Game+, new weapons, outfits, and more. Here's a closer look at everything that's new: Valhalla Protocol https://youtu.be/yRF4IXmNixo The main event of Extended Operations, Valhalla Protocol brings back Bond's signature Aston Martin Valhalla ride for a race against the clock in Slovakia. The track will have four different versions that you can test your driving skills in, and when putting the pedal to the metal isn't enough, you can always rely on its arsenal of guns and missile launchers to help you earn a first-place finish--far better than a boring Formula One race. Photo mode Is that a Great Gatsby meme pose?007 First Light has no shortage of exciting moments, and you can capture them in all their digital glory in the game's new photo mode. Similar to the photo modes found in many modern games, you can set up Bond and use unique filters, custom light setups, exclusive poses, and much more to take the perfect shot. New operation: Jungle Heist Welcome to the Jungle Heist, we've got guns and flames.A new mission for 007 First Light, Jungle Heist tasks Bond with infiltrating a jungle villa, finding out who's concealing the codes to a secret safe, retrieving its contents, and then fighting your way up to the extraction point. New weapons Locked and loaded.Bond's arsenal is also being updated with two new weapons: the Squire Marksman rifle and the Storm 12 shotgun. New outfits For your fashion eyes only.Time to dress for success--or big-budget Hollywood explosions--with a fresh set of Q Division threads. Bond can don some casual clothes with the Leisure Beam outfit, posh it up with the First Class tuxedo, and blend in with the Observant Spy ensemble. New Game Plus Time for a Bond replay.You can replay the entire 007 First Light campaign--which is really good!--and you can also choose to wear different outfits that you've unlocked from your first session with the game. 00 difficulty mode Prepare to die, a lot.Think you've earned your 00 number? You can put your skills to the test with the 00 difficulty mode, which is designed to punish even the smallest mistake. Resources are more limited, enemies are deadly, and the mode is billed as the ultimate challenge for players. IO Interactive has steadily added new content to 007 First Light since it launched in May, and Amazon Game Studios boss Jeff Gattis recently suggested that a sequel is a matter of when, not if. The game reached an impressive milestone of 4 million units sold in August 2026 across PC and consoles--minus Switch 2, as 007 First Light is still MIA on that platform. The Switch 2 edition has been delayed several times, and it's now expected to arrive in March 2027 as IO works on getting it ready for the Nintendo handheld. "As Hollywood seems uncertain about where to take Bond next, IO Interactive’s debut effort is supremely confident," Mark Delaney wrote in GameSpot's 007 First Light review.

title: How Long Is Gears of War: E-Day – Mission List And Hours Played
description: Gears of War: E-Day is almost here--unless you're hopping in a few days early with the Premium Edition--and if you're looking to try out the campaign, you can settle in for a few days of action and chainsaw executions. While Gears of War: E-Day is primarily a linear cover-based shooter, the game also sprinkles in some semi-open-world environments for you to explore between missions, giving you the opportunity to hunt down collectibles, upgrades, and take part in side missions. Here’s how long it’ll take you to beat Gears of War: E-Day. How long to beat Gears of War: E-Day depending on your play style If you tackle the Gears of War: E-Day campaign on normal difficulty, do a little bit of collectibles hunting and take part in the game's non-story missions, expect the campaign to take 10-14 hours to complete. In my own playthrough, I motored through the campaign and finished it in 11 hours, occasionally stopping along the way to track down a hidden item, find an upgrade pack for my arsenal, and take part in a side quest. I'd done roughly 60% of that content before I reached the end, and Gears of War: E-Day has a war journal that provides a very comprehensive list of things you missed in each mission, so you can go back and find them for a completionist run. That's a fairly standard playthrough time for a game in this series, and once you've rolled credits, the various multiplayer modes look like they'll consume plenty of your hours. You can increase the difficulty and spend more time in the campaign, but on higher challenge levels, enemies can be bullet-sponges that quickly burn through your stock of spare lives. Horde Siege looks like an especially enjoyable timesink, as this new take on the Gears of War horde mode revolves around three teams of four players taking on waves of enemies, co-operating with each other to accomplish objectives, and survive against increasingly overwhelming odds. Gears of War: E-Day mission list The campaign for Gears of War: E-Day is spread across five acts, each comprising several chapters. Acts 1 and 5 are the shortest of the bunch, while Acts 2-4 are lengthy, meaty parts of the overall narrative. You could easily do an Act per night, and spread them out over a week. You can see the full list of Acts and Chapters below, and if you ever want to go back to an earlier one to hunt down a missing collectible or gear upgrade, you can easily do so from the main menu. title: Crypto lost $1.26 billion in hacks while bitcoin bulls enjoyed a monster quarter
description: Your day-ahead look for Oct. 1, 2026

title: Synthetic tokenized stocks are bad for American investors
description: U.S. markets are the envy of the world because investors trust that whoever owns a share owns it fully, writes Aaron Kaplan, founder of Promethum. The synthetic models cheapens that trust, shortchanges U.S. investors, and undercuts the issuer-led capital markets model.

title: Tokenized assets don’t always mirror traditional markets, Dune finds
description: Dune found that tokenized markets show different trading patterns from traditional markets, with RWA value reaching $34.5 billion.

title: Bitcoin kicks off new quarter in the old $82,000-$85,000 price range
description: Prices briefly topped $85,000 on Wednesday after weaker-than-expected U.S. inflation cooled bets on Fed rate hikes, But bulls couldn’t hold the move and spot ETFs didn’t help.

title: Bitcoin trapped below $86K as PCE changes cloud inflation reading
description: Bitcoin erased its post-PCE gains as analysts cautioned that methodology changes complicated the lower-than-expected inflation reading.

title: Binance’s EU services face scrutiny over licensing exemption: Report
description: EU regulators are reportedly examining Binance’s use of a MiCA exemption to serve customers as ESMA seeks stronger enforcement powers.

title: Citigroup raises 12-month bitcoin target to $113,000 as ETF inflows resume
description: Citi also raised its 12-month target for ether from from $2,240 to $3,028.

title: MetaMask security incident forces Ethereum staking exits, no funds at risk
description: An Ethereum security researcher estimates about 0.36 ETH in rewards was diverted, while precautionary exits cover validators holding roughly 523,000 ETH.

title: Dogecoin gets DeFi testnet as DogeOS bets miners will eventually secure its apps
description: DogeOS wants to turn DOGE into more than a payments and speculation asset, but its applications still rely on selected operators rather than Dogecoin miners.

title: A Bloody Attack on a FlyDubai Plane Headed to Israel, and a Terrifying Plunge
description: “I don’t deserve to die like this,” said one passenger on Flight 1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv. The motive of the cockpit stabbing remains unknown, officials said.
